newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela qualifies eleven for Sidor sale.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela qualifies eleven for Sidor sale.

text.p: The Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) said Monday that all 11 groups that registered to participate in the sale of state-owned steel company Sidor had qualified to bid for a controlling stake early next year.
The eleven groups include five from Mexico, two from Brazil, one from Japan, one from South Korea, one from Argentina and one from Venezuela.
The Mexican companies which qualified were Hylsamex SA, Imexsa, Sicartsa, Grupo Acero del Norte and Ahmsa and Grupo Siderurgica Panamericana.
From Brazil Usiminas and Companhia Siderurgica Nacional have qualified.

Japan's Kobe Steel Ltd, South Korea's Dongkuk Steel Group, Argentina's Siderar SAIC and Venezuela's Sivensa make up the rest of the qualified companies selected in consultation with U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers which is handling the Sidor sale.
The FIV said the companies will draw lots on Oct 18 to decide in what order they receive access to information on the 1.8 million tonne per year capacity company.
The FIV had specified that interested bidders must have a net worth over $250 million, proven experience in managing similar plants and a production capacity of at least one million tonnes per year.
